runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mostly higher overnight, with the Nikkei 225 adding 0.5% to close at 65,856 as semiconductor-adjacent names caught a bid ahead of Nvidia's Wednesday print. The DAX and FTSE 100 were essentially flat — DAX at 26,136 and FTSE at 10,816 — as European traders digest the latest round of U.S. sanctions on Iran and a breakdown in U.S.-Canada trade talks, both of which injected macro uncertainty into global risk sentiment overnight. Oil retreated modestly (WTI ~$71.80) while the dollar softened and Treasury yields eased to 4.32%, keeping the macro setup relatively benign heading into the U.S. open.

U.S. pre-market futures are constructively bid: S&P 500 futures +0.12%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.85%, and Dow futures nearly flat +0.01%. The divergence between the Nasdaq and Dow reflects market focus squarely on semiconductors and AI names ahead of Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 earnings report Wednesday after the close. Sandisk cleared $1,525 and QQQ reclaimed the $711 level in pre-market trading, signaling the tape is pricing in a strong Nvidia beat. The broader bull thesis is intact but event risk this week is heavy.

The week's two dominant macro catalysts converge Wednesday: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole address (markets are keenly watching for any pivot toward rate cuts or inflation tolerance shifts), and PCE data prints the same morning. Monday's mixed close — SPX -0.28%, Dow +0.26%, Nasdaq -0.76% — was weighed down by chip sanctions fallout and geopolitical noise. Tuesday's early bid suggests those concerns are fading and positioning is rotating back into mega-cap tech ahead of the most consequential earnings print of the summer.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia reports Q2 FY2027 earnings after market Wednesday Aug 26, with consensus expectations high and pre-market positioning firmly bullish.
ideas.thesis: NVDA remains the undisputed AI infrastructure bellwether; any beat on revenue and data center guidance will ignite a sector-wide rally in semis and AI-adjacent names. Supply-demand dynamics for Blackwell remain skewed long, and forward estimates have been trending higher all quarter.
ideas.key_risk: A miss on data center revenue or cautious H2 guidance amid Iran sanctions disrupting chip exports could trigger a sharp reversal given stretched positioning.

sources.label: Seeking Alpha – NVDA Q2 2026 Earnings Call

ideas.catalyst: Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy from Outperform and raised its price target to $641 from $565 on Tuesday.
ideas.thesis: AMD benefits from both the AI inference buildout and the Nvidia halo effect heading into Wednesday's print; the Raymond James upgrade reflects improving conviction on AMD's MI300 datacenter GPU ramp and gaming recovery. A strong Nvidia result would likely lift AMD as the sector's second-derivative play.
ideas.key_risk: If Nvidia disappoints or guides cautiously on AI capex, AMD faces collateral selling despite its independent product cycle.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley upgraded Dynatrace to Overweight from Equal Weight and raised the price target to $65 from $58 on Tuesday August 25.
ideas.thesis: Dynatrace is a high-quality observability platform with durable ARR growth; the Morgan Stanley upgrade reflects improving enterprise software spending signals and DT's competitive positioning against Datadog. AI-driven infrastructure complexity is a secular tailwind for the entire observability category.
ideas.key_risk: Enterprise IT budget scrutiny and macro slowdown fears could compress multiples; broader tech selling on any Nvidia miss would drag DT lower despite company-specific positives.

ideas.catalyst: DKS tumbled 17% after missing Q2 EPS estimates and slashing its full-year profit outlook, signaling consumer discretionary stress in sporting goods.
ideas.thesis: The magnitude of the guidance cut suggests structural margin pressure beyond one bad quarter; promotional environment and inventory normalization headwinds are likely to persist into Q3 and Q4. Sell-side will need to materially reset estimates, creating additional overhang.
ideas.key_risk: A sharp market-wide rally or sector rotation into consumer names could provide a short-term technical bounce, squeezing short positions.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added AON to its August Conviction Buy List, citing 9% above-consensus FCF for 2026-27 and NFP acquisition synergy realization.
ideas.thesis: AON's combination of NFP integration synergies, broker talent investment, and an eventual capital markets recovery create a multi-year earnings growth runway well above what the Street is modeling. The stock trades at a discount to its own historical multiple despite improved earnings quality.
ideas.key_risk: A sharp rates rally or recession fears could compress insurance broker valuations; NFP integration execution risk remains if talent attrition accelerates.

ideas.catalyst: SCI gained 4.9% after reporting strong Q2 2026 results and announcing a major expansion of its share buyback program.
ideas.thesis: SCI is a defensive compounder with pricing power in funeral and cremation services, and the buyback expansion signals management confidence in free cash flow durability. Demographic tailwinds (aging U.S. population) support mid-single-digit volume growth through the decade.
ideas.key_risk: Integration risk from recent acquisitions and any macro-driven decline in discretionary funeral spending upgrades could compress margins.

ideas.catalyst: JEF gained 5.5% Tuesday amid a broader financial sector rally, likely driven by improving capital markets activity and M&A advisory pipeline.
ideas.thesis: Jefferies is a leveraged play on a capital markets recovery; with IPO pipelines (Anthropic, General Atlantic) building and M&A volumes ticking up in August, Jefferies' advisory and underwriting revenues should inflect positively in H2 2026. The stock typically outperforms when deal activity accelerates.
ideas.key_risk: A risk-off event triggered by a Warsh hawkish surprise at Jackson Hole or a Nvidia miss could freeze capital markets and derail the recovery thesis.

ideas.catalyst: KURA surged 10.5% after CEO and President Troy Wilson purchased 100,000 shares of company stock on August 24, 2026.
ideas.thesis: CEO open-market purchases of this size in a micro-cap biotech are among the highest-conviction insider signals; the timing ahead of upcoming data readouts or potential partnership announcements suggests management sees asymmetric upside not reflected in current share price. Kura's oncology pipeline targets hematologic and solid tumor cancers with differentiated mechanisms.
ideas.key_risk: Biotech binary risk remains if pipeline data disappoints; insider purchases do not guarantee regulatory or clinical success.

ideas.catalyst: Kaos Capital, a significant and growing shareholder, issued a letter pushing for an immediate board meeting, nominating two independent directors, and demanding a new M&A-focused board committee at Capricor Therapeutics amid an FDA decision on Deramiocel.
ideas.thesis: Activist pressure combined with an imminent FDA decision on Deramiocel for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy creates a binary-but-asymmetric setup; a positive FDA outcome would substantially increase the company's strategic value and likelihood of an M&A outcome. Activists rarely take this level of public action without conviction in near-term catalysts.
ideas.key_risk: FDA rejection of Deramiocel would significantly impair the thesis; activist campaigns can be protracted and management may resist.

ideas.catalyst: Wolfe Research raised Moderna to Peer Perform from Underperform on Tuesday August 25, signaling an end to institutional selling pressure.
ideas.thesis: Wolfe's upgrade from Underperform removes a key overhang and could trigger short covering; Moderna's mRNA platform has diversification beyond COVID vaccines including RSV, flu, and oncology applications that the market has chronically undervalued. A rotation into defensive biotech amid macro uncertainty could lift the group.
ideas.key_risk: Moderna's revenue trajectory remains challenged by declining COVID booster uptake, and pipeline catalysts are multi-year; the upgrade to Peer Perform (not Buy) limits upside conviction.

deals.headline: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Confidential IPO Disclosure Expected by End of August
deals.description: Anthropic, the AI safety company and developer of the Claude platform, is preparing to make its confidential U.S. IPO filing public as soon as the end of August 2026, advancing a transaction expected to rank among the largest tech IPOs in history. The filing would follow a period of explosive revenue growth driven by enterprise API adoption and Claude-powered products.
deals.impact: High — a successful Anthropic IPO would validate AI infrastructure valuations and provide a benchmark for private AI company pricing across the sector.

deals.headline: General Atlantic Restarts U.S. IPO Plans with JPMorgan Lead
deals.description: General Atlantic, the global growth equity firm, has restarted preparations for a U.S. IPO after shelving earlier listing plans during a weaker capital-markets environment, naming JPMorgan as lead underwriter. The relisting reflects improving market conditions and signals renewed confidence in the IPO window heading into Q4 2026.
deals.impact: Medium — adds to the growing IPO pipeline alongside Anthropic, signaling that the capital markets window is open and benefiting underwriters like Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Jefferies.

deals.headline: Ingenic Semiconductor Lists H Shares on Hong Kong Stock Exchange
deals.description: Ingenic Semiconductor priced its Hong Kong H-share IPO at HKD 102.80 per share, offering approximately 31.29 million shares and raising roughly HKD 3.22 billion (~$410M USD). Ingenic designs processors and connected-device semiconductors, joining a growing wave of mainland Chinese chipmakers seeking liquidity in Hong Kong amid continued U.S. access restrictions.
deals.impact: Medium — reinforces the Hong Kong exchange as a capital-raising destination for Chinese chip companies locked out of U.S. markets; may attract attention to HKEX-listed semiconductor names.

deals.headline: Kaos Capital Launches Activist Campaign at Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR)
deals.description: Kaos Capital disclosed a significant and growing stake in Capricor Therapeutics and issued a public letter demanding an immediate board meeting, nominating two independent directors, and pushing for creation of a new M&A/strategic alternatives committee on the board. The move comes ahead of an imminent FDA decision on Capricor's lead drug Deramiocel for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, with Kaos arguing the company is significantly undervalued and ripe for acquisition.
deals.impact: High for CAPR — activist pressure combined with FDA binary creates a high-volatility setup; positive FDA outcome could accelerate M&A outcome.

deals.headline: Madison Air Agrees to Acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 Billion
deals.description: Madison Air announced a definitive agreement to acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 billion, the largest M&A deal disclosed in August 2026. The transaction combines two HVAC-adjacent industrial companies and is expected to accelerate Madison Air's commercial expansion into data center cooling infrastructure, a segment seeing surging demand driven by AI server buildout.
deals.impact: Medium — highlights industrial M&A activity driven by AI data center infrastructure build; potential read-through for other HVAC/cooling names like Vertiv and Johnson Controls.
